title:
bin/story.sh runs story commands in the caller's CWD, not the repo root --priority high --description ## What
`plugin/claude-code/bin/story.sh` resolves the repo root into `dir` (`dir=$(repo_root)`, line 223) but never `cd`s there. Every `$STORY` invocation — `story show` (232), `story list --ready` (255), `story move --if-state` (269), and the rollback move (174) — therefore runs in whatever directory the caller happened to be in.

## Why it breaks
The story CLI has no `--repo`/`-C`/`--cwd` flag, and `ensure_project` (src/storage.rs:315-323) does NOT walk up ancestors — the project root is always exactly `env::current_dir()`.

## Extent
1. `/story do <id>` invoked from ANY subdirectory of the repo fails with exit 3, 'story project not initialized in this directory; run `story init`'.
2. Worse, invoked from inside an existing dispatched worktree it does not fail — it silently reads the WRONG tracker. `.storyhook/` is version-controlled, so every git worktree carries its own independent copy. `repo_root()` correctly anchors worktree creation to the main repo (it deliberately uses `--git-common-dir`, not `--show-toplevel`), but the ready-gate and the CAS claim are then evaluated against the worktree's own `.storyhook/open/stories/`. The claim can succeed in one checkout while the worktree is created in another.

## Repro
Inside a storyhook-initialized repo, from a tmux session:
  mkdir -p src && cd src && /story do <a-ready-id>
Expected: dispatches. Actual: ok:false, 'story project not initialized in this directory'.

## Last known good
Never worked — present since the verb landed in ed4f23d (PR #42, issue #40).

## Fix
`cd` to `$dir` before any $STORY call (or run them in a subshell anchored there). Regression test: dispatch from a subdirectory.
